solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Light blow to the skull?

parts.note: the skull stands for the head
to lamp someone is slang for to hit them, so a lamp is a blow

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gentle knock on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as an adjective (a soft blow) but is the noun being defined; the blow lands on the skull, so the head comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlamp is the front lamp of a vehicle, or one worn on the forehead, a source of illumination.

clue.text: Clinic initially planned in hot, very large country unfinished

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the rest of the wordplay
something unfinished lacks its final part, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
a European country

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: first letter of planned

explanation.surface: A clinic was originally planned for a big, hot country but never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is the clothing-size label for very large garments; the country is cut short before the first letter of planned slips inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is a medical institution, and clinic is a near synonym for such a place of treatment.

clue.text: Theatre number

parts.note: surface reading: a song or act performed on stage
setter's reading: something that numbs, as used in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song in a show, but read it as numb-er: the thing that makes a patient numb in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug given before surgery removes sensation, so it is literally what numbs a patient in the operating room.

clue.text: Lady Caroline runs American firm in the red

parts.note: Lady Caroline Lamb, the novelist famous for her affair with Byron
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
US abbreviates the United States
CO is short for company

explanation.surface: An aristocrat runs a US company that is losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the red' suggests debt, but the red is the wine being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is an Italian sparkling wine, usually red in colour, so it is a red.

clue.text: Unbottling Emirs' fine wine for cooking

indicators.note: taking something out of its bottle removes the outer casing, so each word loses its outside letters

parts.note: the inside of emirs, without its first and last letters
the inside of fine, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Opening the rulers' good wine to cook with.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirin is a sweet Japanese rice wine used as a seasoning in the kitchen.

clue.text: Refuse to work small child's plaything

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a trike is a tricycle, a child's toy

explanation.surface: A little child refuses to touch a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike is to stop working as a protest, a standard verb synonym.

clue.text: Island rodent turned up bits of skeleton

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters run upward, so they read backwards

parts.note: IS is an abbreviation for island
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: An island rat surfaces with some bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi, plural of tarsus, are the ankle bones, so they are parts of the skeleton.

clue.text: Former President upset Peking somewhat

indicators.note: upset in a down clue tips the letters over, so they read from bottom to top
somewhat means only part of a word is wanted, a run of its letters

parts.note: letters inside the city name

explanation.surface: A former president is somewhat annoyed by Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, a former US President.

clue.text: Chap regularly partaking of beer an' wine

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at a steady interval, every other one

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A man routinely drinks beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's name, and a chap is any man, so a name can stand for a chap.

clue.text: Council efficiently getting to grips with mounting litter

indicators.note: gripping something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ably means competently, efficiently

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means climbing, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: litter is a mess

explanation.surface: A council deals efficiently with a growing litter problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathered body of representatives, such as a regional council.

clue.text: Prison bars might produce one

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a jail
second meaning: a tequila cocktail served in pubs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface links prison and bars as cell bars; the second bars are drinking places serving a tequila slammer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a jail and also names a drink of tequila and mixer banged on the counter.

clue.text: Ship's doctor voided operation following great tidal wave

indicators.note: following places this piece after the next one in the answer

parts.note: a surge is a great rush of sea water

indicators.note: voided means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of operation

explanation.surface: A ship's medic cancelled an operation after a huge wave.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy the ship's doctor carries the title surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval medical officer is titled surgeon, and the word is used for a ship's medic generally.

clue.text: Julius Was Archbishop of Canterbury claims crazy Sun cover

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the setter's name standing for the setter himself, I
RAN CE: the Archbishop of Canterbury heads the CE, the Church of England

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of having been Archbishop and mocks a mad tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves by their pseudonym, so Julius is I. CE is the Church of England, which the Archbishop of Canterbury leads; the Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is protection against loss, and cover is the everyday word for that protection.

clue.text: Problem child

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a point of difficulty or dispute
second meaning: offspring, as in died without children

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a difficult child; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a matter in dispute and also, formally, one's offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Gave up when turret discovered in Dresden exploded

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other before the mixing
something exploded is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dis-covered means its covering is stripped, so the outer letters go

parts.note: turret without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wartime capitulation came after a turret was found among the ruins of bombed Dresden.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to yield or give up, so gave up is the past tense equivalent.

clue.text: Swordsman shot, injured after onset of attack

indicators.note: after puts the mixed piece behind the single starting letter
the onset of something is its very start, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of attack

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fencer was shot and wounded just as the attack began.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, a famous fictional swordsman.

clue.text: Being retired, Karen — a Bahamian — hosts a Caribbean dance

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters run backwards
hosts means the words contain the answer within them

parts.note: a run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Karen, a retired Bahamian woman, puts on a Caribbean dance evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow dance and song form from Havana, Cuba, an island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Honourable medal King introduced to former Crown territory

parts.note: Hon is the abbreviation for Honourable

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so the single letter goes into the medal word

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or honour
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king gives a medal to an honourable figure in a former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: The K goes in after the first G of GONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hong Kong was a British colony until its handover to China in 1997, so it is a former Crown territory.

clue.text: North-eastern rock icon's providing sanctuary for fifty young birds

parts.note: NE abbreviates north-east

indicators.note: giving sanctuary means sheltering someone inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Sting, the rock singer, with the possessive S
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A northern rock star's estate shelters fifty chicks.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting, from Newcastle in the north-east, was lead singer of the Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestlings are chicks too young to leave the nest, so they are young birds.

clue.text: Tech giant stocks each day looked attractive

indicators.note: to stock something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Apple, the technology company
EA is the abbreviation for each
D abbreviates day

explanation.surface: A tech firm's shop sold items that seemed appealing each day.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to be attractive or interesting, so appealed means seemed attractive.

clue.text: Lawyer attending jousting competition has forgotten uniform

parts.note: at as in at a party, attending

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a tourney is a medieval jousting tournament
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns up to a jousting event without the right outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a legal representative, the American term for a lawyer.

clue.text: Cry following son being forced into Victorian labour

definitions.note: 'being' is a noun here: a person

indicators.note: following places the cry after the single letter

parts.note: S abbreviates son
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A son weeps at being made to work as a Victorian child labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb, but it is a noun, a creature: one made to climb chimneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian chimney sweeps used small boys forced to climb flues, so a sweep was such a person.

clue.text: Bird having wings of cicada stuck in gullet

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a maw is a throat or gullet

indicators.note: the wings of something are its two sides, its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of cicada

explanation.surface: A bird has an insect's wings caught in its throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Very serious traffic queue heading north over Reading, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a traffic jam is a queue of vehicles
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
reading is one of the three Rs of basic schooling

explanation.surface: A long tailback heading north towards Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the town on the M4, but it is one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means significant or grave, as in a major incident, so very serious.

clue.text: Crossing a street? We refuse

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so the outer word straddles the inner pieces

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ST abbreviates street

explanation.surface: Someone declines an invitation to cross the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is unwanted material, and refuse (stressed on the first syllable) means rubbish.

clue.text: Learning Dutch during weeklong exercises

indicators.note: during means within a period, so one piece goes inside the other
exercises, as a verb, works the letters around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A language course in Dutch runs as a week of drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning, as a noun, means acquired knowledge, as in a person of great learning.

clue.text: Newspaper leader coming from former Murdoch editor

indicators.note: the leader of a name is its first letter, and coming from it means it is taken off

parts.note: Piers Morgan edited the Murdoch-owned News of the World

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial by a man who once worked for Murdoch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a newspaper editorial, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a periodical that speaks for a group, so a newspaper can be called one.

clue.text: "No NHS job will be scrapped" — ex-British PM, unforgettably

indicators.note: scrapped means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
job with its last letter removed
surface padding: a wry comment on the ex-PM, giving no letters

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's pledge that no health service jobs would go.
explanation.walkthrough: The B of job is dropped, perhaps hinted by 'be scrapped' read as B scrapped; 'unforgettably' is a wry comment. Boris Johnson was UK Prime Minister 2019-22.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson was a British Prime Minister, now former, so he is an ex-PM.

clue.text: Smell from rubbish not OK

indicators.note: not means without, so the two letters are taken away

parts.note: hokum is nonsense
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unpleasant odour from the bins.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a hum is an unpleasant odour, so it means a smell.

clue.text: Officer classes beginning to leave

parts.note: genera, plural of genus, are classes in biology

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of leave

explanation.surface: An officer's lessons are starting to break up.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a high-ranking army officer.

clue.text: Wartime leader breaks from melancholy

indicators.note: breaks from means a piece is broken out of the words, a run of their letters

parts.note: a run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A wartime leader escapes from depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Erwin Rommel, the Desert Fox, was a German field marshal and commander in the Second World War.

clue.text: Biased… indeed so corrupt!

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are put in a distorted order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a decision was biased and crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: One-sided means favouring one party unfairly, which is what biased means.
